messages.content:
<question>
Can I knock down a wall or otherwise change the layout of the flat I rent in Spain without my landlord's agreement?
</question>

<answer>
No. Under Spanish residential tenancy law, a tenant may not carry out works that change the layout or configuration of the dwelling or its accessories without the landlord's written consent [1]. In no case may a tenant carry out works that reduce the stability or safety of the dwelling [1]. If the landlord did not authorise the works, he may, without prejudice to his power to terminate the contract, require the tenant to restore the dwelling to its former state at the end of the lease, or he may keep the change without compensating the tenant [1]. If the works reduced the stability of the building or the safety of the dwelling, the landlord may require immediate restoration [1].
</answer>

<reference>
No. The tenant may not carry out, without the landlord's written consent, works that change the configuration of the dwelling or of its accessories, and in no case works that reduce the dwelling's stability or safety (art. 23.1 of the Ley de Arrendamientos Urbanos). If the landlord did not authorise them, then, without prejudice to his power to terminate the contract, he may require at the end of the lease that the tenant restore things to their former state, or keep the change without compensating the tenant; and if the works reduced the building's stability or the dwelling's safety, he may require immediate restoration (art. 23.2).
</reference>

The criterion is correctness against a reference answer that a person checked against the statute. The answer passes if it states the same rule as the reference on what the question asks: the same obligation, right, period, amount, condition or exception that the reference relies on. Extra correct detail is fine. Leaving out a condition or exception that the reference treats as essential fails, and so does any statement that contradicts the reference. Wording, order and length do not matter. If the reference says part of the question cannot be answered from the law, the answer must leave that part open too, not fill it in.

In your reasoning, name the rule the reference states, then say whether the answer states it, leaves part of it out, or contradicts it.

response.text: {"reasoning":"The reference states: no tenant works changing the configuration of the dwelling or accessories without written consent; never works reducing stability or safety; if unauthorised, landlord (without prejudice to termination) may require restoration at end of lease or keep the change without compensation; if stability/safety reduced, immediate restoration may be required. The answer states all of these points: written consent requirement, the absolute bar on stability/safety-reducing works, the end-of-lease restoration or keep-without-compensation options, and immediate restoration for stability/safety cases. It cites art. 23 implicitly as [1] and doesn't omit any essential condition. Wording differs but the rules match.","verdict":"pass"}
